en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Chapter on Similes,
Section on the Ocean.
8. The Question on the Factors of the Pilot “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘three factors of a pilot must be adopted,’ which are those three factors that must be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, a pilot steers a ship day and night, constantly, continuously, with diligence, restraint, and effort;”
In the same way, Great King, a yogi practicing yoga, while directing his mind, must direct it day and night, constantly and continuously, with heedfulness, exertion, and wise attention.
This, Great King, is the first quality of a helmsman that should be adopted.
And this was said, Great King, by the Blessed One, the God beyond gods, in the Dhammapada:
“Be devoted to heedfulness,
guard your own minds;
pull yourself out from the difficult ford.”
"Like an elephant stuck in the mud.
Furthermore, Great King, whatever is in the great ocean—whether good or bad—all that is known to the navigator;

even so, Great King, by a practitioner who is a yogi, the wholesome and the unwholesome, the blameworthy and the blameless, the inferior and the superior, and the dark and the bright with their counterparts, must be discerned.
This, Great King, is the second quality of the helmsman that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the helmsman gives a seal to the machine, saying, ‘Let no one touch the machine.

In the same way, Great King, the practitioner of yoga should apply the seal of restraint to the mind, saying, ‘May you not think any evil, unwholesome thought. This, Great King, is the third quality of the helmsman that should be adopted.
"Great King, this was also said by the Blessed One, the God above gods, in the excellent Saṃyutta Nikāya:
‘Monks, do not direct your thoughts toward evil and unwholesome things, namely:
sensual thought, thought of ill will, and thought of cruelty.’"
The eighth question: on the factor of the guide.
